title: Console surface triage: scope carveout for cost + traces (cost mosaic)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures a surgical scope reduction for Redwood Console observability surface focused on dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown. The goal is to define an actionable MVP cutset we can implement in the next cycle to deliver a coherent, performant surface that surfaces cost and basic tracing without incurring the full telemetry ingestion and card set planned in the PRD. This is a pragmatic rebaseline that preserves critical signals for customers while deferring heavy aggregation, per-token attribution, and full trace retention to later releases.
background: The PRD for Console Observability targeted a broad surface: per-route cost breakdown, route-level traces with full span-level flamegraphs, unlimited historical drilldowns, and fine-grained token-level costing. After infra and storage budget reviews, we must reduce scope to meet performance SLOs and delivery timelines. Engineering requested clarity on minimum acceptable features and measurable acceptance criteria to avoid last-minute scope creep.
scope_changes: 1) Dashboard: limit to three compact cards for MVP: (a) Top-10 routes by spend (30d), (b) 95th latency summary + error rate, (c) Unit-cost trend (7d). Defer: per-route timeline drilldown beyond 30d, per-endpoint heatmaps, and custom card creation. 2) Cost breakdown: provide aggregated cost buckets only (model compute, infra, cache savings) and top-10 route attribution. Defer per-token attribution and line-item token sampling. 3) Tracing: ship adaptive sampling with two windows: (a) full capture for P0 errors and flagged traces, (b) 5% sampled successful traces with span-level limits (max 200 spans). Defer: full flamegraph UI and span-search across long time windows. 4) Telemetry storage: cap retention for the MVP to 14 days for sampled traces and 90 days for aggregated metrics; defer long-term archival integration. 5) Rollouts: default experience will use aggregated cards; advanced features hidden behind feature flags for Dedicated/Private customers only.
decisions:
- Adopt 'cost mosaic' naming for the compact aggregated cost view to emphasize aggregated buckets and top routes.
- Use adaptive trace sampling implemented in runtime as a lightweight agent to avoid a separate ingestion pipeline.
- Prioritize Dashboard render performance; target default view <1.2s for cold load.
- Expose a 'Request a deeper trace' CTA that triggers on-demand capture for a single customer session (future work: automated on-demand capture flow).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard default view loads under 1.2s on 95th percentile for internal perf lab conditions.
2) Cost mosaic exposes: aggregated cost buckets (compute, infra, cache savings) and top-10 routes for last 30d with correct totals within 2% of backend billing snapshot.
3) Trace sampling policy implemented: 100% of P0 errors captured with full spans up to 200 spans, successful requests sampled at 5% with span limit. Demonstrate in test harness with synthetic traffic.
4) Storage retention policies enforced: sampled traces retained 14 days; aggregated metrics retained 90 days.
5) Feature flags exist for deferred capabilities and can be enabled per-org.
6) Product and UX review signed off on compact card designs and messaging for deferred capabilities.
7) Documentation draft for 'cost mosaic' explaining what is shown and known limitations is in Confluence and linked.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Customers expecting per-token attribution will be disappointed. Mitigation: Clear UI messaging and support article; prioritize a roadmap item for per-token attribution.
Risk: Sampling may miss intermittent regressions. Mitigation: Full capture on P0 errors and an on-demand capture CTA; engineering to add low-latency rule to trigger capture for error spikes.
Risk: Aggregated numbers differ from billing. Mitigation: Implement reconciliation job and add acceptance threshold (2% tolerance) with alert to PM/finance if exceeded.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha behind feature flag for Redwood staff and selected beta customers (1 week). Phase 2: Public beta for self-serve customers with opt-in (2 weeks). Phase 3: GA with feature-flag default on for accounts under trial limits; Dedicated accounts get opt-in to advanced features. Communications: product changelog, support KB, and an in-console tooltip explaining retention and sampling.

metrics_and_signals:
- Dashboard cold-load P95 < 1.2s.
- Cost mosaic delta vs billing < 2%.
- Trace capture rate for P0 errors = 100%.
- Sampled trace volume within storage budget target (projected < 40% of initial telemetry estimate).
- Beta NPS and support tickets about missing per-token detail tracked; target <= 10 tickets in first month.
notes:
- Engineering provided a cost estimate showing full scope would require ~3x storage and 2x ingestion throughput; hence the surgical cut.
- Design suggested an expandable 'More details' flyout for each card that can link to premium features.
- Legal asked to confirm retention window for GDPR; we agreed 14 days for traces (MVP) and will document in policy.
- This ticket replaces earlier broader PRD acceptance criteria with a pragmatic ship-minimum approach.
customer_notes: Communicate: MVP will surface top spenders and high-level cost buckets. For customers needing per-token billing now, provide a support path for Dedicated/Private purchasing conversation.
